entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: You became acquainted with Madarame's[n]pupil by chance?

entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: That's a little too convenient. It makes me[n]wonder if you're even telling the truth.

entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: So be it. What I want to know most[n]is your method.

entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: It's true that Madarame was an[n]unforgivable criminal worthy of[n]the scorn thrown at him.

entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: He was an adult who cultivated his[n]own fame and fortune by sacrificing[n]the livelihood of children...

entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: But he'd been covering his tracks for[n]years. How did you uncover the truth in[n]such a short span of time?

entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: Fine. Let's suppose that people's hearts[n]can be changed by stealing their Treasure,[n]like you've said.

entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: If so, a different suspicion arises.

entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: People have gone mad or lost[n]consciousness, never to recover...[n]like the subway accident in April.

entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: Depending on how you look at it, that[n]could be taken as a phenomenon for a[n]sudden change of heart too.

entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: ...Were you related to those as well?

entries.speaker: Sae
entries.en: Fine. Let's get back to Madarame's case.[n]Keep it concise, and stick to the facts.
